query: Prior studies of Al-containing Cr–Co–Fe–Ni alloys showed that composition and thermal history can substantially alter constituent phases and transformation behavior, but they did not establish a predictive explanation of phase stability across the relevant thermal regime or adequately connect it to composition-dependent thermodynamic instability. Given the competing thermodynamic and kinetic factors in multicomponent alloys, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains what governs phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially in a high-temperature BCC state and why? State a controlled comparison and baseline, predicted observations, boundary conditions, prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially in a high-temperature BCC solid solution, phase stability during cooling and aging is governed primarily by Al–Ni/Co chemical short-range order (CSRO) that seeds B2-type ordering in the BCC lattice. Where the pre-existing Al–Ni/Co CSRO exceeds a critical nearest-neighbor order parameter, B2 nuclei form readily and lower the free energy enough to destabilize the single-phase BCC, driving partitioning of Cr to a Cr-rich BCC/sigma matrix. If CSRO is suppressed (randomized BCC), the nucleation barrier to B2 remains high and the BCC state persists metastably or decomposes more slowly. Thus, the magnitude of Al–Ni/Co CSRO is the structural mediator that determines whether thermodynamic instability (miscibility gap plus ordering enthalpy) manifests as rapid ordering/decomposition or metastable retention of BCC.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase BCC solid solution of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 held at high temperature above any B2 long-range order onset, with minimal long-range order and tunable Al–Ni/Co CSRO via pre-annealing.
generation.intervention: Set different initial Al–Ni/Co CSRO levels before identical aging: (a) homogenize at very high temperature to minimize CSRO, then ultrafast quench (randomized BCC); (b) pre-anneal slightly below the order–disorder onset to enhance Al–Ni/Co CSRO, then quench (CSRO-seeded BCC).
generation.conditions: Pre-anneal (b): 1050–1150°C for 2–8 h, then quench; homogenize (a): ≥1200–1250°C for 1–2 h, then ultrafast quench. Subsequent identical isothermal aging at 700–850°C for 0.5–24 h in vacuum/inert atmosphere; cooling rates controlled (e.g., oil quench vs furnace cool).
generation.structural_mediator: Nearest-neighbor Al–Ni/Co CSRO (quantified by Warren–Cowley parameters) that promotes B2-type local motifs in the BCC lattice and associated coherency strain fields at B2/BCC interfaces.
generation.mechanism: Strongly negative Al–Ni/Co pairwise mixing enthalpy in BCC drives local ordering toward B2. When initial CSRO is high, the nucleation barrier to B2 is lowered, enabling rapid formation of B2 precipitates/domains that reduce the system’s free energy. Concurrently, unfavorable Cr–(Ni,Co) interactions and the resulting miscibility gap promote partitioning of Cr to a Cr-rich matrix (BCC or sigma, depending on time/temperature). If initial CSRO is low, ordering requires larger composition fluctuations and longer-range diffusion of Al/Ni, so the BCC solid solution remains metastable or transforms more slowly. Thus, thermodynamic instability (ordering plus demixing) manifests only when the CSRO mediator passes a threshold set by temperature and prior thermal history.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the randomized-BCC baseline, the CSRO-seeded material will: (i) show earlier onset of B2 long-range order (detectable superlattice reflections) during 700–850°C aging; (ii) develop a higher B2 volume fraction at fixed time; (iii) exhibit stronger Al–Ni/Co partitioning into B2 and stronger Cr partitioning into the matrix; and (iv) show faster hardness/strength increase consistent with ordered B2 formation. Direction: increased CSRO increases B2 fraction and ordering kinetics. Approximate size: the difference in B2 fraction after identical aging is expected to be substantial (qualitatively, tens of percent change is plausible), but the exact magnitude is uncertain without direct measurement.
generation.baseline: Randomized BCC achieved by homogenization at ≥1200–1250°C followed by ultrafast quench; initial Al–Ni/Co CSRO near zero; under 700–850°C aging, B2 superlattice intensity grows slowly and BCC retention persists longer; Cr-rich sigma only appears after prolonged aging if at all.
generation.boundary: Applies within the 600–900°C regime where diffusion of Al/Ni/Co is active and B2 ordering is thermodynamically favorable; above the order–disorder temperature, CSRO is erased and B2 does not persist; at very low temperatures, kinetics may be too sluggish for ordering. Composition sensitivity: significantly lower Al or Ni/Co content will reduce the ordering drive; significantly higher Cr may promote sigma formation that competes with B2. Extremely rapid quenching can trap metastable BCC regardless of prior CSRO.
generation.uncertainty: Exact critical CSRO threshold, quantitative B2 fraction differences, and the onset temperature for sigma formation in this specific composition are uncertain without direct measurement. Magnetism and magnetic transitions could modulate free energies near certain temperatures, but their contribution here is not constrained by the available information.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 with identical composition and grain size: Set A (randomized) homogenized at 1250°C for 2 h then water/ice brine quenched; Set B (CSRO-seeded) annealed at 1100°C for 6 h then quenched. Verify initial CSRO using diffuse scattering or atom probe nearest-neighbor statistics. Age both sets isothermally at 800°C for varied times (0.5, 2, 8, 24 h). Characterize phase fractions and ordering.
measurements: X-ray or neutron diffraction: B2 superlattice peak intensities (e.g., {100} in B2) and Rietveld-estimated B2 volume fraction versus time
Atom probe tomography: Al–Ni/Co nearest-neighbor correlation coefficients and partitioning profiles (Al/Ni/Co enrichment in ordered domains; Cr enrichment in matrix)
TEM/SAED: direct imaging of ordered B2 domains and interface coherency with BCC
SAXS/SANS or diffuse scattering: quantify CSRO before aging and its evolution
Microhardness/nanoindentation: hardness evolution correlating with ordering
EBSD/XRD: detection of sigma phase onset and fraction (if present) versus time
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If Set B does not exhibit faster B2 ordering kinetics and higher B2 fraction than Set A at all aging times, despite verified higher initial Al–Ni/Co CSRO, or if B2 formation rate/fraction is uncorrelated with measured Al–Ni/Co CSRO while sigma or other phases form with similar kinetics in both sets, the hypothesis is falsified. Additionally, if eliminating CSRO (via high-T homogenization) does not raise the B2 nucleation barrier (i.e., both sets show indistinguishable B2 superlattice intensity evolution), the hypothesis is falsified.
